recorded.prompt:q-mapmulti-labels: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapmulti-labels: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapmulti-labels: Page lines 138-145: 'the result type R appears only in the type of sink ... javac doesn't infer it from the values the body passes to accept, and the List<String> on the left doesn't reach back through .toList(), so R becomes Object' and 'Only when mapMulti's result goes straight to a Stream<String> (an assignment, a return, an argument) does the target type decide R; add .filter(s -> s.isEmpty()) after it and s is an Object again.' The NoWitness compile error (lines 132-136) shows rejection. A reader picks b. Small gap: the page shows the failure through filter/toList, not a String::toUpperCase method reference on Object, so the exact failing stage is inferred from 's is an Object again', not shown.
recorded.prompt:q-shift-roster: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shift-roster: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shift-roster: Page lines 190-210: 'sorted() without a comparator needs Comparable elements, and nothing checks that until the terminal operation compares two of them'; the Ticket record run prints 'pipeline built' then a ClassCastException at toList(), while 'one ticket: [Ticket[...]]' succeeds; 'One ticket sorts without complaint ... so a one-row test passes.' Summary line 326-327 repeats it. Shift is a plain record like Ticket, so a reader picks a.

recorded.pass:q-guest-coupons: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-guest-coupons: Page lines 62-73: 'A function given to flatMap may return null: the javadoc says an empty stream is used instead', with the run 'flatMap: [pen, ink, pad, pen, clip]' for a function returning null on the empty order. Reference table line 352: 'a null stream counts as empty'. Two + zero + one coupons gives three codes; a reader picks a.
recorded.prompt:q-block-trade: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-block-trade: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-block-trade: Page lines 169-173: 'sorted is stateful: it can't know which element comes first until it has seen the last, so it buffers everything and emits only when the source is exhausted. A findFirst() or limit(3) after it stops nothing upstream.' Summary line 325-326 and Reference table line 345 ('never returns; the same with findFirst()'). The stream ends at market close, so nothing arrives until then; a reader picks a.

recorded.outcome:q-guest-coupons:b: Refuted by lines 62-73: flatMap substitutes an empty stream for null; the null staying as an element is what map does ('The same null returned to map stays in the stream as an element'), not flatMap.

recorded.prompt:q-guest-coupons:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-guest-coupons:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-guest-coupons:d: Refuted, somewhat indirectly: the map run shows '[pen, null, pad]' (line 72) and line 59-60 says orElse(null) 'would put a null in the list', so lists keep nulls; and here no null element reaches toList() at all, since flatMap uses an empty stream. Caveat: the page's snippets omit their terminal operation, so it never names toList() explicitly as keeping nulls. Partly true: the outcome (three codes) is correct; only the reason is wrong.

recorded.outcome:q-block-trade:b: Refuted by line 171-172: 'A findFirst() or limit(3) after it stops nothing upstream', and the Reference table: sorted then findFirst 'never returns' on an endless source. Partly true: findFirst does short-circuit in general (Design Note line 375-376).
recorded.prompt:q-block-trade:c: the page and the question, and nothing else

recorded.outcome:q-block-trade:c: Refuted by 'emits only when the source is exhausted' (line 171) and the run 'sorted().limit(3): nothing after 2 s, 66,503,114 elements pulled' (line 182); summary: 'on an endless stream it never returns'.
recorded.prompt:q-block-trade:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-block-trade:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-block-trade:d: Reason refuted: the sorted trace (lines 161-166) shows a single 'after sorted 10' line before 'findFirst -> 10', so findFirst takes one element; Design Note line 375-376 says the push model 'is what lets limit and findFirst stop an endless source'; the wait comes from sorted. Partly true: the outcome (nothing until market close) matches the correct answer; only the reason is wrong.
